deep.reconstruction:
The page proves a lemma used later for eigenvalue and singular-value inequalities, in the setting of Fredholm theory and nuclear operators of 1953. The lemma is the weak-majorization theorem. Let α_1≥…≥α_n and β_1≥…≥β_n satisfy α_1+…+α_k ≤ β_1+…+β_k for all k; in case b) the full sums are equal. Then φ(α) ≤ φ(β) for every symmetric convex increasing function φ (in case b) monotonicity is not needed).

The proof runs as follows.
(i) The previous page notes that a finite convex function on R^n is a supremum of affine functions L_k(t)=Σ a_i t_i + b_k, because its epigraph is closed and convex.
(ii) This page shows that if φ is increasing, each minorant L_k ≤ φ has all a_i ≥ 0. Suppose a_i<0, fix t_j for j≠i and let s=t_i→−∞. Then L_k→+∞, while φ stays bounded above, being increasing in s. This contradicts L ≤ φ.
(iii) If φ is symmetric, every permuted function σL_k, with (σL)(t)=L(t_{σ^{-1}1},…,t_{σ^{-1}n}), is also ≤ φ. Hence (7): φ = sup_k sup_{σ∈S_n} σL_k.
(iv) So it suffices to prove (8): sup_σ (σL)(α) ≤ sup_σ (σL)(β) for a single affine L with a_i ≥ 0. The right side is ≤ φ(β). One may take b=0.
(v) The quantity sup_σ Σ a_{σi} α_i = sup_σ Σ a_i α_{σi} is attained when a is arranged in the same order as α. This is the rearrangement inequality. So one reduces to a_1≥…≥a_n≥0 and proves Σ a_iα_i ≤ Σ a_iβ_i.
(vi) The next page finishes with Abel summation (9): Σ a_iβ_i = Σ_{k<n} (a_k−a_{k+1})(β_1+…+β_k) + a_n(β_1+…+β_n). Each term compares termwise, using a_n≥0 and either Σα≤Σβ, or equality in case b).
(vii) The next page then applies this to sequences ρ_i, σ_i, apparently a multiplicative or log-majorization setting such as eigenvalues versus singular values (Weyl). It derives the inequality f(1/σ_1,…,1/σ_n) ≤ f(1/ρ_1,…,1/ρ_n) for reciprocal sequences.

This is the classical Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya / Karamata / Tomić–Weyl majorization inequality, proved by the standard supporting-hyperplane, symmetrization and Abel-summation route.
errors: The transcription reads 'L(t)→0 si t_i→−∞'. Mathematically it must be L(t)→+∞ when a_i<0, which then contradicts L≤φ with φ bounded above. Otherwise the argument is correct.
The use of (ii) needs φ finite and increasing in each variable. Then φ is bounded above as t_i→−∞ with the other variables fixed, which is fine. No real gap.
The reduction in (v) implicitly uses the rearrangement inequality without proof. It is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a self-contained re-proof of the classical Tomić–Weyl / Karamata majorization inequality, presumably for eigenvalue and singular-value estimates of nuclear or p-summing operators. The mathematics is correct but entirely standard and already in the literature by 1949. It is of historical interest only, showing Grothendieck re-deriving Weyl-type inequalities for himself in 1953.
